questions.question: Which of the following shows the correct formula for acceleration?

options.text: acceleration = change in velocity / time taken

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**acceleration = change in velocity / time taken**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acceleration** is defined as the rate at which an object changes its **velocity**. An object is accelerating if it is changing its velocity.
 
• The formula for **acceleration** is the **change in velocity** divided by the **time taken** for that change to occur. Mathematically, it is represented as **a = (v - u) / t**, where **v** is the final velocity, **u** is the initial velocity, and **t** is the time. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• According to **Newton's Second Law of Motion**, the relationship between **force**, **mass**, and **acceleration** is **Force = mass × acceleration**. Therefore, **acceleration = Force / mass**. The provided option suggests acceleration equals force multiplied by mass. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Acceleration is the change in velocity per unit of time, not the product of the two. Multiplying **velocity** by **time** would result in **displacement** (for constant velocity), not acceleration. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The formula **distance / time** is the definition for **speed**, whereas **displacement / time** is the formula for **velocity**. Acceleration requires looking at the change in those rates over time. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SI Unit:** The **Standard International (SI) unit** for **acceleration** is the **meter per second squared**, commonly written as **m/s²**. This unit signifies how many meters per second the velocity changes every second.
 
• **Vector Quantity:** **Acceleration** is a **vector quantity**, meaning it has both **magnitude** and **direction**. A change in either the speed or the direction of motion results in acceleration.
 
• **Types of Acceleration:**
 
 
• **Uniform Acceleration:** When an object's velocity changes by equal amounts in equal time intervals. A classic example is an object in **free fall** near the **Earth's surface**, where it accelerates at approximately **9.8 m/s²**.
 
• **Non-Uniform Acceleration:** When the velocity of an object changes by unequal amounts in equal intervals of time.
 
 
 
• **Deceleration:** When the **acceleration** acts in the opposite direction to the **velocity**, the object slows down. This is often referred to as **negative acceleration**, **retardation**, or **deceleration**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Graphical Representation:** In a **Velocity-Time (v-t) graph**, the **slope** of the line represents the **acceleration** of the object. A steeper slope indicates a higher magnitude of acceleration, while a horizontal line indicates **zero acceleration** (constant velocity).
 
• **Instantaneous vs. Average Acceleration:** **Average acceleration** is the total change in velocity over a specific period, whereas **instantaneous acceleration** is the acceleration of an object at a specific **moment in time**.
 
• **Circular Motion:** Even if an object moves at a **constant speed** in a circle, it is still **accelerating** because its **direction** is constantly changing. This is known as **centripetal acceleration**.

2

questions.question: What is the function of the nuclear membrane in a cell?

options.text: It stores digestive enzymes for chromosomal activities.
It prevents the entry of gases and water molecules into the nucleus.
It provides energy for nuclear division during mitosis.
It regulates the transfer of material between nucleus and cytoplasm.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It regulates the transfer of material between nucleus and cytoplasm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **nuclear membrane**, also referred to as the **nuclear envelope**, is a **double-layered** biological membrane that encloses the **genetic material** of **eukaryotic cells**.
 
• It serves as a physical barrier that separates the contents of the **nucleus** (the **nucleoplasm**) from the **cytoplasm**.
 
• The membrane is perforated by numerous **nuclear pores**, which act as gatekeepers. These pores **regulate the transfer of materials**, such as **RNA**, **ribosomal subunits**, and **proteins** (like **polymerases** and **histones**), between the nucleus and the cytoplasm. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• The function of storing **digestive enzymes** is performed by **lysosomes**, which are often called the "suicidal bags" of the cell, rather than the nuclear membrane. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The nuclear membrane is **selectively permeable**; it does not prevent the entry of essential **water molecules** or **dissolved gases** like **oxygen** and **carbon dioxide**, which are necessary for cellular respiration and nuclear metabolic processes. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Energy required for **nuclear division** and other cellular processes during **mitosis** is generated by the **mitochondria** in the form of **ATP** (Adenosine Triphosphate), not by the membrane itself. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of the Nuclear Envelope:**
 
 
• It consists of two **lipid bilayer** membranes: the **outer nuclear membrane** and the **inner nuclear membrane**.
 
• The **outer membrane** is continuous with the **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)** and is often studded with **ribosomes**.
 
• The **inner membrane** is lined by the **nuclear lamina**, a network of **intermediate filaments** (lamins) that provides structural support and helps organize **chromatin**.
 
 
 
• **The Nuclear Pore Complex (NPC):**
 
 
• Each **nuclear pore** is a massive protein complex that manages the bidirectional trafficking of macromolecules. 
 
• Small molecules (less than **30-60 kDa**) can diffuse passively, but larger molecules require specific **transport receptors** like **importins** and **exportins**.
 
 
 
• **Role in Cell Division:**
 
 
• During the **prophase** of **mitosis**, the nuclear membrane breaks down into small vesicles to allow the **spindle fibers** to access the **chromosomes**.
 
• In the **telophase**, the vesicles fuse to reform the nuclear envelope around the two sets of daughter chromosomes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Perinuclear Space:** The gap between the inner and outer membranes is called the **perinuclear space**, which is typically about **20 to 40 nm** wide.
 
• **Discovery:** While the **nucleus** was first described by **Robert Brown** in **1831**, the detailed structure of the double-layered nuclear membrane was only clearly understood after the advent of the **electron microscope** in the **20th century**.
 
• **Protection:** By sequestering the **DNA**, the nuclear membrane protects the genome from being damaged by metabolic reactions occurring in the cytoplasm and ensures that **transcription** and **translation** are spatially and temporally separated in eukaryotes.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT explained by the law of gravitation?

options.text: Artificial satellites revolving around the Earth
Falling of raindrops to the Earth
The electrostatic attraction between two charged bodies

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The electrostatic attraction between two charged bodies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation**, formulated by **Sir Isaac Newton** in **1687**, states that every particle of matter in the universe attracts every other particle with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their **masses** and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
• **Artificial satellites revolving around the Earth**: These satellites are maintained in their orbits because the Earth's **gravitational force** provides the necessary **centripetal force** required for circular or elliptical motion. Without this pull, satellites would fly off into space in a straight line. ***Hence, statement 1 is explained by the law of gravitation.***
 
• **Tides in oceans**: The periodic rise and fall of sea levels, known as tides, are primarily caused by the **gravitational pull** exerted by the **Moon** and, to a lesser extent, the **Sun** on the Earth's hydrosphere. ***Hence, statement 2 is explained by the law of gravitation.***
 
• **Falling of raindrops to the Earth**: Raindrops are pulled toward the center of the Earth due to **Earth's gravity**. This force acts on the mass of the water droplets, causing them to accelerate downwards once they become heavy enough to overcome atmospheric updrafts. ***Hence, statement 3 is explained by the law of gravitation.***
 
• **The electrostatic attraction between two charged bodies**: This phenomenon is governed by **Coulomb's Law** (proposed in **1785**), which deals with the force between **electric charges** rather than masses. While it follows an inverse-square law similar to gravity, it is a fundamentally different force of nature. ***Hence, statement 4 is NOT explained by the law of gravitation.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Universal Gravitational Constant (G)**:
 
 
• The value of **G** was first experimentally determined by **Henry Cavendish** in **1798**.
 
• The accepted value of **G** is approximately **6.674 x 10^-11 Nm²/kg²**. It is a scalar quantity and remains constant throughout the universe.
 
 
 
• **Coulomb's Law vs. Gravitational Law**:
 
 
• **Coulomb's Law** states that the force between two point charges is proportional to the product of the **charges** (q1, q2) and inversely proportional to the square of the distance (r²) between them.
 
• Unlike **gravitation**, which is **always attractive**, **electrostatic force** can be either **attractive** (between opposite charges) or **repulsive** (between like charges).
 
• The electrostatic force is significantly stronger than the gravitational force; for example, the electric force between a proton and an electron is about **10^39 times stronger** than the gravitational force between them.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Inverse Square Law**: Both gravitation and electrostatics follow the **inverse square law**, meaning the intensity of the force decreases rapidly as the **distance** between the objects increases.
 
• **Central Forces**: Both forces are **central forces**, meaning they act along the line joining the centers of the two bodies.
 
• **Planetary Motion**: The law of gravitation explains **Kepler's Laws** of planetary motion, describing how planets move in elliptical orbits around the Sun.
 
• **Weight vs. Mass**: **Mass** is the amount of matter in an object (measured in **kg**), while **weight** is the **gravitational force** acting on that mass (measured in **Newtons**). Weight varies depending on the local gravitational acceleration (g), which is approximately **9.8 m/s²** on Earth.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Pitch has no relation with frequency.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**High pitch means high frequency.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **pitch** of a sound is the brain's perception of the **frequency** of a sound wave. **Frequency** is defined as the number of vibrations or cycles per **second**.
 
• There is a **direct relationship** between pitch and frequency. A higher frequency results in a **high-pitched** or shrill sound, while a lower frequency results in a **low-pitched** or grave sound.
 
• High pitch means low frequency: This statement is incorrect because frequency and pitch are positively correlated. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• High pitch means high frequency: This statement accurately describes the physical relationship where faster vibrations (higher frequency) produce a higher perceived pitch. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Pitch has no relation with frequency: This is false because frequency is the primary physical attribute that determines the pitch of a sound. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Low pitch means high frequency: This is incorrect as high frequency leads to high pitch, not low pitch. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The unit of **frequency** is **Hertz (Hz)**. If an object vibrates **50 times** in one second, its frequency is **50 Hz**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Sound:**
 
 
• **Loudness:** Unlike pitch, loudness depends on the **amplitude** of the vibration. It is measured in **decibels (dB)**. When the amplitude is large, the sound produced is loud.
 
• **Quality (Timbre):** This characteristic allows us to distinguish between two sounds of the same **pitch** and **loudness**, such as the difference between a **violin** and a **flute**.
 
 
 
• **Frequency Ranges:**
 
 
• **Infrasonic Sound:** Sounds with frequencies below **20 Hz** are called infrasonic. Elephants and whales communicate using these frequencies.
 
• **Audible Range:** The human ear can typically hear frequencies between **20 Hz and 20,000 Hz (20 kHz)**.
 
• **Ultrasonic Sound:** Frequencies above **20,000 Hz** are called ultrasound. Animals like **bats** and **dolphins** use ultrasound for navigation and hunting.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Examples of Pitch:**
 
 
• A **bird** makes a high-pitched sound (high frequency), whereas a **lion** makes a low-pitched roar (low frequency), although the roar is much louder (high amplitude).
 
• The voice of a **woman** generally has a higher frequency and is higher pitched than that of a **man**.
 
• A **drum** vibrates with a low frequency, producing a low-pitched sound, while a **whistle** has a high frequency, producing a high-pitched sound.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Pitch:**
 
 
• The pitch of a stringed instrument (like a **guitar**) can be increased by increasing the **tension** in the string or decreasing its **length**.
 
• In wind instruments, the pitch is changed by altering the length of the **vibrating air column**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Consider the following statements and select the correct option.

Statement A: A neutralisation reaction occurs when an acid reacts with a base.
Statement B: Water and salt are formed during neutralisation.

options.text: Both statements A and B are correct.
Statement A is correct but B is incorrect.
Statement A is incorrect but B is correct.
Both statements A and B are incorrect.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both statements A and B are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Neutralization** is a type of **chemical reaction** in which an **acid** reacts with a **base** to form **salt** and **water**.
 
• In this reaction, the **acidity** of the acid and the **alkalinity** of the base are **neutralized**, often resulting in a solution that is closer to a **neutral pH**. ***Hence, statement A is correct.***
 
• The primary products of a **neutralization reaction** are always a **salt** (an ionic compound) and **water (H2O)**. ***Hence, statement B is correct.***
 
• The reaction is generally **exothermic** in nature, meaning **heat energy** is released during the process, which can cause an increase in the **temperature** of the reaction mixture.
 
• The general **chemical equation** for this process is represented as: **Acid + Base → Salt + Water + Heat**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Daily Life Applications of Neutralization:**
 
 
• **Indigestion:** To relieve acidity in the **stomach** caused by excess **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)**, **antacids** like **Milk of Magnesia** (which contains **Magnesium hydroxide**) are used to neutralize the acid.
 
• **Ant Sting:** An ant's sting contains **formic acid**. The effect can be neutralized by rubbing **moist baking soda** (**sodium hydrogen carbonate**) or **calamine solution** (**zinc carbonate**) on the skin.
 
• **Soil Treatment:** If the **soil** is too acidic, it is treated with bases like **Quick lime** (**calcium oxide**) or **Slaked lime** (**calcium hydroxide**). If it is too basic, **organic matter** is added, which releases acids to neutralize the base.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Examples:**
 
 
• A common laboratory example is the reaction between **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** and **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)**. This produces **Sodium chloride (NaCl)**, which is common table salt, and **water**.
 
 
 
• **Indicators in Neutralization:**
 
 
• **Phenolphthalein** is frequently used as an **indicator**. In a **basic** solution, it gives a **pink** color, but it becomes **colorless** when the solution becomes **acidic** or **neutral** during the neutralization process.
 
 
 
• **Nature of Salt:**
 
 
• The salt produced may be **acidic**, **basic**, or **neutral**. For instance, a **strong acid** reacting with a **strong base** produces a **neutral salt** with a **pH** of **7**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Presbyopia is correct?

options.text: It is corrected only by concave lenses.
It usually occurs in young children.
It occurs due to weakening of ciliary muscles and loss of lens flexibility.
The near point becomes less than 25 cm.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It occurs due to weakening of ciliary muscles and loss of lens flexibility**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Presbyopia** is a common vision condition that occurs with **aging**, where the eye gradually loses its ability to focus clearly on nearby objects.
 
• It is primarily caused by the **gradual weakening** of the **ciliary muscles** and the diminishing **flexibility** (elasticity) of the **crystalline lens**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The power of **accommodation** of the eye usually decreases with **age**. For most people, the **near point** gradually recedes and becomes **greater than 25 cm**, making it difficult to read comfortably without corrective glasses. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• Unlike conditions like Myopia, **Presbyopia** is not typically found in **young children**; it usually becomes noticeable in individuals in their **early to mid-40s** and continues to worsen until around age **65**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• This condition is generally corrected using **convex lenses** (for reading) or **bifocal lenses** if the person also suffers from Myopia. **Concave lenses** are used to correct Myopia (nearsightedness), not Presbyopia alone. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Myopia (Nearsightedness):**
 
 
• In this defect, a person can see nearby objects clearly but cannot see distant objects distinctly.
 
• It occurs due to **excessive curvature** of the eye lens or **elongation** of the eyeball.
 
• It is corrected using a **concave lens** of suitable power.
 
 
 
• **Hypermetropia (Farsightedness):**
 
 
• A person with hypermetropia can see distant objects clearly but cannot see nearby objects distinctly.
 
• The **near point** for the person is farther away from the normal near point (**25 cm**).
 
• It arises because the **focal length** of the eye lens is too long or the eyeball has become too small.
 
• It is corrected by using a **convex lens** of appropriate power.
 
 
 
• **Astigmatism:**
 
 
• This defect arises when the **cornea** is not spherical in shape, leading to different **curvatures** in different planes.
 
• It results in objects appearing blurred or distorted at all distances.
 
• It is typically corrected using **cylindrical lenses**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Power of Accommodation:** The ability of the eye lens to adjust its **focal length** is called accommodation. When muscles are relaxed, the lens is thin and its focal length increases (for distant objects). When **ciliary muscles** contract, the lens becomes thick, and the focal length decreases (for nearby objects).
 
• **Bifocal Lenses:** Sometimes a person suffers from both **Myopia** and **Hypermetropia/Presbyopia**. Such people require **bifocal lenses**. A common type of bifocal lens consists of both concave and convex lenses. The **upper portion** is a **concave lens** (facilitates distant vision), and the **lower part** is a **convex lens** (facilitates near vision).
 
• **Modern Solutions:** Nowadays, vision defects can also be corrected with **contact lenses** or through **surgical interventions** such as **LASIK** (Laser-Assisted In Situ Keratomileusis).
 
• The **least distance of distinct vision** for a normal young adult eye is **25 cm**, and the **far point** is **infinity**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the magnetic field around a current carrying solenoid?

options.text: The direction of magnetic field associated with the solenoid can be reversed by reversing the direction of current flowing through it.
The field associated with the solenoid can be increased by decreasing the number of turns in the solenoid.
The field in the core of the solenoid decreases from one end of the other end.
The field line pattern of the solenoid resembles the magnetic field line pattern of a straight current carrying wire.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The direction of magnetic field associated with the solenoid can be reversed by reversing the direction of current flowing through it**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **solenoid** is defined as a coil of many circular turns of **insulated copper wire** wrapped closely in the shape of a **cylinder**. When current passes through it, it behaves like a magnet.
 
• The **direction of the magnetic field** produced by a **solenoid** depends entirely on the **direction of the electric current** flowing through the coils. By **reversing the current**, the polarity (North and South poles) of the solenoid flips, thereby reversing the field direction. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• The **magnitude** of the magnetic field (**B**) is **directly proportional** to the **number of turns per unit length (n)** and the **current (I)**. Therefore, the field associated with the solenoid can be **increased by increasing** the number of turns, not decreasing them. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• Inside a long **solenoid**, the **magnetic field lines** are in the form of **parallel straight lines**. This indicates that the **magnetic field is uniform** at all points inside the core of the solenoid, meaning it does not decrease or increase from one end to the other. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*
 
• The **magnetic field line pattern** produced by a current-carrying **solenoid** is remarkably similar to the **magnetic field of a bar magnet**, with one end behaving as a **magnetic North pole** and the other as a **South pole**. It does not resemble the circular field pattern of a **straight current-carrying wire**. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is The direction of magnetic field associated with the solenoid can be reversed by reversing the direction of current flowing through it.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Factors affecting Magnetic Field Strength:**
 
 
• **Current (I):** The strength of the **magnetic field** is **directly proportional** to the **current** flowing through the wire. Increasing the current in **Amperes** leads to a stronger field.
 
• **Number of Turns (N):** A **solenoid** with a higher **density of turns** produces a more intense **magnetic field** because the field of each individual turn adds up.
 
• **Core Material:** Placing a **soft iron core** inside the solenoid significantly increases the **magnetic induction**. This setup is commonly known as an **electromagnet**.
 
 
 
• **Rules and Resemblance:**
 
 
• **Right-Hand Thumb Rule:** This rule is used to find the direction of the **magnetic field**. If the fingers of the right hand wrap around the solenoid in the **direction of current**, the thumb points towards the **North pole**.
 
• **Clock Face Rule:** If the current in a face of the solenoid is in a **clockwise direction**, that face acts as a **South pole**; if **anti-clockwise**, it acts as a **North pole**.
 
• **Similarity to Bar Magnets:** Like a **bar magnet**, the **magnetic field lines** of a solenoid emerge from the **North pole** and enter the **South pole** outside the magnet, forming closed loops.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Applications of Solenoids:**
 
 
• **Electromagnets:** Used in **electric bells**, **cranes** for lifting scrap metal, and **relays**.
 
• **Medical Equipment:** High-end medical devices like **MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging)** machines use large solenoids to generate strong **uniform magnetic fields**.
 
• **Automotive:** Solenoids are used as **starters** in vehicles to engage the engine during ignition.
 
 
 
• **Key Comparison:**
 
 
• A **permanent magnet** (like a steel bar) retains its magnetism, whereas a **solenoid** acts as a magnet only as long as the **electric current** is flowing.
 
• The **strength** of a permanent magnet cannot be changed easily, but the strength of a **solenoid** can be varied by changing the **current** or the **number of turns**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: What is the formula unit mass of sodium chloride (NaCl)?
questions.solution: The correct answer is __**58.5u**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The **formula unit mass** of a substance is the sum of the **atomic masses** of all atoms in a formula unit of a compound. • For compounds that consist of **ions** (ionic compounds), the term **formula unit mass** is used instead of **molecular mass** because these substances do not consist of discrete molecules. • **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)** is a classic example of an **ionic compound**. It consists of **Sodium (Na+)** cations and **Chloride (Cl-)** anions arranged in a crystal lattice. • The **atomic mass** of **Sodium (Na)** is **23 u**. • The **atomic mass** of **Chlorine (Cl)** is **35.5 u**. • The **formula unit mass** of **NaCl** is calculated as: **1 × 23 u + 1 × 35.5 u = 58.5 u**. • ***Hence, the correct answer is 58.5u.***

questions.question: The cleansing action of soap is due to which of its properties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ability to form micelles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Soap molecules** are **sodium** or **potassium salts** of long-chain **fatty acids** (like stearic, palmitic, or oleic acid) that possess a dual nature: a **hydrophilic** (water-loving) head and a **hydrophobic** (water-fearing) tail.
 
• The **hydrophilic head** is the **ionic part** (**-COONa+**), which interacts with water, while the **hydrophobic tail** is a long **hydrocarbon chain** that interacts with oils, grease, and dirt.
 
• When soap is dissolved in **water**, the molecules arrange themselves into spherical aggregates known as **micelles**. In a micelle, the hydrophobic tails point towards the center to trap **grease**, while the hydrophilic heads face outwards toward the water. ***Hence, the statement regarding the ability to form micelles is correct.***
 
• The **cleansing action** occurs because the oily dirt is collected in the center of the micelle. When the water is agitated, these micelles, containing the trapped dirt, are washed away, leaving the surface clean.
 
• Soap is generally the product of a **weak acid** and a **strong base**, making it slightly **alkaline** (basic) in nature, but its primary function of cleaning is purely a result of its **surfactant** properties rather than being a "strong base" or "strong acid". ***Hence, statements 1 and 2 are incorrect.***
 
• The **melting point** of soap is a physical property determined by the length of the carbon chain and the type of cation used; it does not dictate the chemical mechanism of removing dirt. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Saponification:** This is the chemical process used to manufacture soap. It involves the **hydrolysis** of fats or oils (triglycerides) using a strong alkali like **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)** for hard soaps or **Potassium Hydroxide (KOH)** for soft soaps.
 
• **Emulsification:** Soap acts as an **emulsifier**. Since oil and water do not mix, soap allows them to form a stable **emulsion**, enabling the oil to be suspended in water and rinsed off.
 
• **Surface Tension:** Soap molecules reduce the **surface tension** of water. By breaking the cohesive forces between water molecules, soap allows the water to "wet" the surface and the fabric fibers more effectively.
 
• **Critical Micelle Concentration (CMC):** This is the specific **concentration** of surfactants above which micelles start to form. Cleaning becomes efficient only once this concentration is reached in the solution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hard Water Interaction:** Soap does not work effectively in **hard water**, which contains high levels of **Calcium (Ca2+)** and **Magnesium (Mg2+)** ions. These ions react with soap to form an insoluble precipitate called **scum**.
 
• **Difference between Soaps and Detergents:** Unlike soaps, **synthetic detergents** are **sodium salts of alkyl hydrogen sulphates** or **alkyl benzene sulphonates**. Detergents are superior because they do not form scum with hard water and can be used in **acidic mediums**.
 
• **Biodegradability:** Most traditional soaps are **biodegradable** because the hydrocarbon chains are straight. However, some older synthetic detergents with branched chains were non-biodegradable and caused **water pollution**.
 
• **History:** The use of soap-like materials dates back to **2800 BC** in ancient **Babylon**, where they combined fats with wood ash (a source of alkali).
</ul

questions.question: If an object is placed at a distance 'u' from a convex lens, 'u' ________.

options.text: depends on the type of image

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**is taken as negative**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the **object** is always placed to the **left of the lens**. This ensures that the **incident light** from the object falls on the lens from the **left-hand side**. 
• All distances measured to the **right of the optical center** (along the direction of incident light) are taken as **positive**, while all distances measured to the **left of the optical center** (against the direction of incident light) are taken as **negative**. 
• Since the object is always placed on the left side, the **object distance (u)** is measured from the **optical center** to the left. Therefore, **u** is **always taken as negative** for both **convex** and **concave lenses**. 
• This convention is fundamental for solving numerical problems using the **lens formula** and ensuring consistency in **optical calculations**. ***Hence, the correct answer is is taken as negative.*** 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Convex Lens (Converging Lens):** 
• A **convex lens** is thicker at the middle than at the edges. It **converges** a beam of parallel light rays falling on it. 
• The **focal length (f)** of a **convex lens** is **positive** because the **principal focus** lies on the right side of the lens. 
• It can form both **real and virtual images** depending on the position of the object. When the object is placed beyond the **focus (F)**, the image is **real and inverted**. If placed between **F and the optical center**, the image is **virtual and erect**. 
• **Concave Lens (Diverging Lens):** 
• A **concave lens** is thinner at the middle than at the edges. It **diverges** parallel rays of light. 
• The **focal length (f)** of a **concave lens** is **always negative** as the focus is considered to be on the left side. 
• It always forms a **virtual, erect, and diminished image**, regardless of the object's distance. 
• **Lens Formula and Magnification:** 
• The **Lens Formula** is expressed as **1/v - 1/u = 1/f**, where **v** is the image distance, **u** is the object distance, and **f** is the focal length. 
• **Magnification (m)** is the ratio of the **height of the image (h')** to the **height of the object (h)**, which is also equal to **v/u**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Power of a Lens:** The **power (P)** of a lens is the reciprocal of its **focal length (f)** measured in **meters** (P = 1/f). The **SI unit** of power is the **Dioptre (D)**. A **convex lens** has **positive power**, while a **concave lens** has **negative power**. 
• **Image Distance (v) Rules:** For a **real image**, **v** is **positive** (formed on the opposite side of the object). For a **virtual image**, **v** is **negative** (formed on the same side as the object). 
• **Height Convention:** Heights measured **upwards** and perpendicular to the principal axis are **positive** (erect images), while heights measured **downwards** are **negative** (inverted images). </ul

questions.question: Which component is used in a circuit to increase resistance and limit current?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Resistor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **resistor** is a passive **two-terminal** electrical component that implements **electrical resistance** as a circuit element. Its primary function is to **reduce current flow** and, at the same time, act to lower voltage levels within circuits.
 
• In accordance with **Ohm’s Law**, the current (**I**) flowing through a circuit is inversely proportional to the **resistance** (**R**) for a given voltage (**V**). This means that by **increasing the resistance**, one can effectively **limit the current**. ***Hence, the resistor is the component used for this purpose.***
 
• Resistors work by converting electrical energy into **heat energy** through a process known as **Joule heating**. This occurs as electrons collide with the **atoms** of the resistive material, losing **kinetic energy** in the process.
 
• The standard unit of resistance is the **Ohm**, which is symbolized by the Greek letter **Ω**. Components are manufactured with specific **resistance values** ranging from less than one ohm to several million ohms (**megohms**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Switch:**
 
 
• A **switch** is a device designed to **interrupt** the flow of electrons in a circuit or to divert it from one conductor to another.
 
• It operates in two primary states: **Open** (breaking the circuit, zero current) and **Closed** (completing the circuit, allowing current).
 
• While a switch controls whether current flows or not, it is not used to **gradually limit** or adjust the amount of resistance in the way a resistor does.
 
 
 
• **Battery:**
 
 
• A **battery** is a **source of electric power** consisting of one or more **electrochemical cells** with external connections.
 
• It provides the **potential difference** (voltage) necessary to drive current through a circuit.
 
• In a circuit diagram, the battery is the **active component** that supplies energy, whereas the resistor is a **passive component** that consumes or limits it.
 
 
 
• **Lamp:**
 
 
• An electric **lamp** (or light bulb) is a **load** that converts electrical energy into **visible light** and **infrared radiation** (heat).
 
• While a lamp possesses **inherent resistance**, its primary application is **illumination**, not the administrative control of current levels for other components.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ohm's Law Formula:** The relationship between the three fundamental electrical quantities is defined by the formula **V = I × R**, where **V** is voltage in **volts**, **I** is current in **amperes**, and **R** is resistance in **ohms**.
 
• **Fixed vs. Variable Resistors:** **Fixed resistors** have a set resistance that cannot be changed. In contrast, **variable resistors**, such as **potentiometers** or **rheostats**, allow the user to adjust the resistance value to vary the **volume**, **brightness**, or **speed** of an appliance.
 
• **Power Rating:** Every resistor has a **wattage rating** (e.g., **1/4 watt**, **5 watts**) which specifies the maximum **power** it can dissipate without burning out. This is calculated using the formula **P = I²R**.
 
• **Resistor Color Code:** Small resistors typically use a series of **colored bands** to denote their **numerical value** and **tolerance**. For example, a **gold** band usually signifies a **5% tolerance**.

questions.question:
A mass of 3 kg is lifted to a height of 12 m. What is the value of potential energy at the given height?

(Take g = 10 { m/s}² )
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**360.0 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potential Energy (PE)** is the energy held by an object because of its **position** relative to other objects, stresses within itself, its electric charge, or other factors.
 
• In this specific case, we are calculating **Gravitational Potential Energy**, which is the energy an object possesses due to its **height** in a gravitational field.
 
• The formula to calculate the **Potential Energy** of an object is given by **PE = m × g × h**, where **m** is the **mass**, **g** is the **acceleration due to gravity**, and **h** is the **height**.
 
• Given the values in the question:
 
 
• **Mass (m)** = **3 kg**
 
• **Height (h)** = **12 m**
 
• **Acceleration due to gravity (g)** = **10 m/s²**
 
 
 
• Substituting these values into the formula: **PE = 3 kg × 10 m/s² × 12 m**.
 
• The calculation yields **3 × 120 = 360**. Since the units for energy in the **SI system** is **Joules (J)**, the result is **360.0 J**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 360.0 J.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Units of Energy:** The standard **International System of Units (SI)** unit for energy and work is the **Joule (J)**. One **Joule** is defined as the work done by a force of **one Newton** acting through a distance of **one meter**.
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem:** The **potential energy** gained by the object is exactly equal to the **work done** to lift it to that height. When an object is lifted at a constant speed, the **applied force** equals the **weight (mg)**, and the work done is **Force × Displacement (mg × h)**.
 
• **Conservation of Energy:** According to the **Law of Conservation of Energy**, energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed. If the **3 kg** mass were dropped from **12 m**, its **potential energy** would gradually convert into **Kinetic Energy (KE)** as it falls, reaching **360 J** of **Kinetic Energy** just before hitting the ground.
 
• **Factors Affecting PE:** **Gravitational Potential Energy** is directly proportional to the **mass** of the object and its **height** above the reference point. If the **mass** were doubled, the **potential energy** would also double.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reference Level:** **Potential energy** is always measured relative to a **reference point** (usually the ground). If the reference point changes, the value of the **potential energy** changes, although the **difference** in energy between two heights remains the same.
 
• **Scalar Quantity:** Energy is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has **magnitude** but no **direction**. This distinguishes it from **vectors** like **velocity** or **force**.
 
• **Dimensional Formula:** The dimensional formula for **Potential Energy** (and all forms of energy/work) is **[ML²T⁻²]**.
 
• **Elastic Potential Energy:** Apart from gravitational, another common type is **Elastic Potential Energy**, which is stored in objects like **springs** or **rubber bands** when they are stretched or compressed, calculated using the formula **1/2 kx²**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a major condition for successful beekeeping?

options.text: Availability of flowering plants throughout the year

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Availability of flowering plants throughout the year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Beekeeping**, also known as **Apiculture**, is the maintenance of honeybee colonies, commonly in hives, by humans. The success of this practice is heavily dependent on the surrounding environment, specifically the **pasturage**.
 
• **Pasturage** refers to the **flowering plants** available to the bees for **nectar** and **pollen** collection. The **Availability of flowering plants throughout the year** ensures a continuous food supply, which is critical for the survival of the colony and the production of honey. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **quality** and **taste** of honey are determined by the type of flowers available. A diverse range of flora allows bees to produce better quality honey.
 
• Growing crops like **wheat** and **rice** does not support beekeeping because these are **wind-pollinated** (anemophilous) crops and do not produce the **nectar** required by bees. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• While bees are **pollinating insects**, their "presence" is the result of beekeeping; the primary condition for the bees to thrive is the food source (flowers), not the presence of other pollinators. ***Hence, statement 3 is not the major prerequisite.***
 
• The **use of pesticides** is actually a major threat to beekeeping. Chemical pesticides can be **toxic** to bees, leading to **Colony Collapse Disorder (CCD)** and high mortality rates in the hive. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Honey Bee Species:**
 
 
• Common species used in India include **Apis cerana indica** (Indian bee), **Apis dorsata** (Rock bee), and **Apis florea** (Little bee).
 
• The **Apis mellifera** (Italian bee) is frequently introduced for **commercial honey production** because of its **high honey collection capacity** and the fact that it stings less and stays in a given beehive for long periods.
 
 
 
• **Bee Colony Structure:**
 
 
• A typical honeybee colony is highly organized and consists of three types of individuals: **one Queen** (the only fertile female), a few hundred **Drones** (fertile males), and thousands of **Worker bees** (sterile females).
 
• **Worker bees** perform all tasks including foraging for **nectar**, building the comb, and protecting the hive.
 
 
 
• **Products of Beekeeping:**
 
 
• **Honey:** A natural food source rich in **iron**, **calcium**, and **sugars**. It is widely used in indigenous systems of medicine.
 
• **Beeswax:** Secreted by the abdominal glands of worker bees, it is used in the manufacture of **cosmetics**, **polishes**, and **pharmaceuticals**.
 
• **Royal Jelly:** A nutrient-rich substance fed to larvae and adult queens, often used as a dietary supplement.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Ecological Importance:**
 
 
• Bees are vital **pollinators** for many crops like **sunflower**, **mustard**, **apple**, and **pear**. Keeping beehives in crop fields during the **flowering period** increases pollination efficiency and improves the **yield** of both the crop and honey.
 
• The **Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)** in India promotes beekeeping through initiatives like the **Honey Mission** (launched in **2017**) to provide employment to rural youth and farmers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• An **Apiary** is a place where beehives are kept for commercial or research purposes. For a successful apiary, it should be located in a place where there is **adequate pasturage** within a **1 to 2-kilometer radius**.
 
• **Seasonal Management:** Beekeepers must provide **artificial feeding** (sugar syrup) during the **dearth period** (when flowers are scarce) to ensure the colony does not starve.
 
• The **National Beekeeping and Honey Mission (NBHM)** is a central sector scheme launched under the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** package to achieve the goal of a **'Sweet Revolution'** in India.
</ul

questions.question: How are the metals in the middle of the activity series usually extracted?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**By reduction using carbon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The metals in the middle of the **activity series**, such as **Iron (Fe)**, **Zinc (Zn)**, **Lead (Pb)**, and **Copper (Cu)**, are moderately reactive. They are usually found in nature as **sulphides** or **carbonates**.
 
• Since it is easier to extract a metal from its **oxide** rather than its sulphides or carbonates, these ores are first converted into metal oxides. This is achieved through processes like **Roasting** (for sulphide ores) and **Calcination** (for carbonate ores).
 
• After conversion, the **metal oxides** are reduced to the corresponding metals using suitable **reducing agents** such as **carbon** (in the form of **coke**). For example, when **Zinc Oxide (ZnO)** is heated with **carbon**, it is reduced to metallic **Zinc (Zn)**.
 
• The chemical reaction for this process is: **ZnO + C → Zn + CO**. This method is efficient and cost-effective for metals with medium reactivity. ***Hence, the correct answer is By reduction using carbon.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Extraction of High Reactivity Metals:**
 
 
• Metals at the top of the activity series, such as **Potassium (K)**, **Sodium (Na)**, **Calcium (Ca)**, **Magnesium (Mg)**, and **Aluminium (Al)**, are very reactive.
 
• These metals cannot be reduced by **carbon** because they have a higher affinity for **oxygen** than carbon does.
 
• They are extracted through **electrolytic reduction** (**electrolysis**) of their molten chlorides or oxides. For instance, **Sodium** is obtained by the electrolysis of molten **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**.
 
 
 
• **Extraction of Low Reactivity Metals:**
 
 
• Metals at the bottom of the activity series are very unreactive and often found in a **native state** (free state), like **Gold** and **Silver**.
 
• Some, like **Mercury**, can be extracted by **heating alone**. For example, **Cinnabar (HgS)**, an ore of mercury, is heated in air to first convert it into **Mercuric Oxide (HgO)**, which then reduces to **Mercury** upon further heating.
 
 
 
• **Use of Displacement Reactions:**
 
 
• Sometimes, highly reactive metals like **Sodium**, **Calcium**, or **Aluminium** are used as **reducing agents** to displace metals of lower reactivity from their compounds.
 
• An example is the **Thermite Reaction**, where **Iron Oxide (Fe2O3)** is reacted with **Aluminium** powder to produce molten iron, commonly used to join railway tracks.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Roasting:** The process of heating **sulphide ores** strongly in the presence of **excess air** to convert them into oxides.
 
• **Calcination:** The process of heating **carbonate ores** strongly in **limited air** (or absence of air) to convert them into oxides.
 
• **Activity Series:** A list that ranks metals in **descending order** of their **chemical reactivity**, which dictates the metallurgical method required for extraction.
</ul

questions.question: The measurable quantity 'Density' may be represented in the SI unit of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**kilograms per cubic metre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Density** is a fundamental physical property defined as the **mass** of a substance per **unit volume**. It indicates how tightly **matter** is packed together within a specific space.
 
• The mathematical formula to determine density is expressed as **Density = Mass / Volume**. This relationship shows that density is **directly proportional** to mass and **inversely proportional** to volume.
 
• In the **International System of Units (SI)**, **mass** is measured in **kilograms (kg)** and **length** is measured in **metres (m)**. Consequently, the unit for **volume** is derived as the **cubic metre (m³)**.
 
• By combining these base units, the **SI unit** for density is derived as **kilograms per cubic metre**, which is written symbolically as **kg/m³**.
 
• Density is considered an **intensive property**, meaning the value remains constant regardless of the **size** or **quantity** of the material being measured, provided the **temperature** and **pressure** are constant. ***Hence, the correct answer is kilograms per cubic metre.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **CGS Units**: In the **Centimetre-Gram-Second (CGS)** system, density is frequently expressed in **grams per cubic centimetre (g/cm³)**. This unit is commonly used in **chemistry** and **laboratory** settings.
 
• **Conversion Factor**: It is important to note that **1 g/cm³** is equivalent to **1000 kg/m³**. For example, if a substance has a density of **2.5 g/cm³**, its SI value is **2500 kg/m³**.
 
• **Density of Water**: The **density of pure water** is a standard reference point, valued at **1000 kg/m³** (or **1 g/cm³**) at a temperature of **4 degrees Celsius**. This is the temperature where water reaches its maximum density.
 
• **Relative Density**: This quantity, also known as **Specific Gravity**, is the ratio of the density of a substance to the density of a reference material (usually **water**). Because it is a ratio, it is **dimensionless** and has **no units**.
 
• **Common Materials**: Different materials exhibit widely varying densities; for instance, **Air** has a very low density of approximately **1.2 kg/m³** at sea level, while **Iron** has a much higher density of about **7,874 kg/m³**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Effect of Temperature**: Generally, as the **temperature** of a substance increases, its particles move faster and spread apart, increasing the **volume** and thereby **decreasing the density**.
 
• **Effect of Pressure**: Increasing the **pressure** on a substance, particularly **gases**, forces the particles closer together. This reduction in volume leads to an **increase in density**.
 
• **Buoyancy and Floating**: According to **Archimedes' Principle**, an object will **float** if its density is **less than** the density of the liquid it is placed in, and it will **sink** if its density is **greater**.
 
• **Measuring Instruments**: Scientists use specific tools like **hydrometers** to measure the density of liquids and **pycnometers** to determine the density of solids or liquids with high precision.
 
• **Mercury**: This liquid metal is exceptionally dense, with a value of approximately **13,600 kg/m³**, making it much heavier than an equal volume of water.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes binary fission from multiple fission in unicellular organisms?

options.text: Binary fission requires spores, but multiple fission does not.
Binary fission occurs only in multicellular organisms, while multiple fission occurs in unicellular ones.
Binary fission produces two daughter cells, whereas multiple fission produces many daughter cells at once.
Binary fission results in many daughter cells, while multiple fission forms only two.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Binary fission produces two daughter cells, whereas multiple fission produces many daughter cells at once**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Binary fission** is a method of **asexual reproduction** where a single-celled parent organism divides into **two** new daughter cells that are nearly equal in size.
 
• **Multiple fission** is a process where the parent cell divides into **many** daughter cells simultaneously, often as a survival mechanism during **unfavorable conditions**.
 
• Statement 1 suggests that **binary fission** requires **spores**. This is false because **spore formation** is a separate asexual method used by organisms like **fungi** (e.g., **Rhizopus**) and **ferns**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 2 claims **binary fission** occurs in **multicellular organisms**. In reality, it is the primary mode of reproduction for **prokaryotes** (like **bacteria**) and certain **unicellular eukaryotes** (like **Amoeba**). Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.</stro

questions.question: A car’s odometer shows 3000 km at the beginning of a journey and 3200 km at the end. If the journey takes 4 hours, what is the car’s average speed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net distance = End reading − Start reading

Net distance = 3200 − 3000 = 200 km

Average speed = Distance ÷ Time

Average speed = 200 ÷ 4 = 50 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 50 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Odometer reading at start = 3000 km

Odometer reading at end = 3200 km

Total journey time = 4 hours

Formula used: Average speed = (Total Distance covered) ÷ (Total Time taken)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2c822858ff588f2859ee4158e7d4369427b9f2cc56f122f98a5674e9aff59180.png] 
⇒ Total Distance = Final Odometer Reading − Initial Odometer Reading
⇒ Total Distance = 3200 − 3000 = 200 km
⇒ Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time
⇒ Average Speed = 200 ÷ 4
⇒ Average Speed = 50 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 50 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If a journey covers two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed is 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Odometer vs. Speedometer

An odometer measures the total distance traveled by the vehicle, while a speedometer measures the instantaneous speed.</p

questions.question: Which of the following statements about asexual reproduction is INCORRECT?

options.text: Fission is a method of asexual reproduction.
It involves the fusion of male and female gametes.
It produces offspring that are genetically identical clones of the parent.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It involves the fusion of male and female gametes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Asexual reproduction** is a mode of reproduction that involves **only one parent**. The offspring produced are biological copies of the parent organism because there is no mixing of genetic material from two different individuals. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• One of the primary characteristics of asexual reproduction is that it **does not involve the fusion of male and female gametes**. The process of gamete formation and their subsequent fusion (fertilization) is the hallmark of **sexual reproduction**. In asexual reproduction, the single parent undergoes cell division to produce offspring. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Fission** is a common method of asexual reproduction widely observed in **unicellular organisms**. It can be **Binary Fission**, where a cell divides into two equal halves (e.g., **Amoeba**), or **Multiple Fission**, where a cell divides into many daughter cells simultaneously (e.g., **Plasmodium**). ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• This process produces offspring that are **genetically identical clones** of the parent. Because the offspring inherit the exact **DNA** of the single parent through **Mitosis**, they are morphological and genetic carbon copies. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• Asexual reproduction is typically **rapid** and requires **less energy** compared to sexual reproduction, allowing organisms to increase their population size quickly in favorable environmental conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Asexual Reproduction:**
 
 
• **Budding**: A small **bud** or outgrowth develops on the parent body, which eventually detaches to become a new individual. Examples include **Yeast** and **Hydra**.
 
• **Fragmentation**: The parent body breaks into several pieces, and each fragment grows into a complete new organism. This is common in **Spirogyra** and some **flatworms**.
 
• **Regeneration**: This is the ability of an organism to regrow lost body parts or form a whole new organism from a small fragment. **Planaria** is a classic example of high regenerative capacity.
 
• **Spore Formation**: Organisms like **Fungi** (e.g., **Rhizopus**) and some **ferns** produce microscopic reproductive structures called **spores** that germinate into new individuals under favorable conditions.
 
• **Vegetative Propagation**: A form of asexual reproduction in **plants** where new plants are produced from vegetative parts like **roots, stems, or leaves** (e.g., **Potato tubers**, **Onion bulbs**, and **Bryophyllum** leaf buds).
 
 
 
• **Key Differences:**
 
 
• In **Sexual Reproduction**, two parents are involved, **Meiosis** occurs to form haploid gametes, and there is significant **genetic variation** due to crossing over.
 
• In **Asexual Reproduction**, there is no **evolutionary variation** unless a mutation occurs, as the offspring are identical to the parent.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Clone Definition**: In biology, a **clone** refers to a group of cells or an entire organism that is genetically identical to the unit from which it was derived. In asexual reproduction, the term is used because the **nuclear DNA** remains unchanged from parent to offspring.
 
• **Occurrence**: Asexual reproduction is prevalent in **prokaryotes** (like **Bacteria** and **Archaea**), many **protists**, **fungi**, and even some **invertebrate animals** and **plants**.
 
• **Mitosis**: This is the underlying cellular mechanism for asexual reproduction. During **Mitosis**, the parent cell replicates its **chromosomes** and segregates them into two identical nuclei for the daughter cells.
 
• **Significance**: While it lacks the variation needed for rapid evolution in changing environments, it is highly efficient for colonizing **stable habitats** where the parent's traits are already well-adapted for survival.
</ul
